event: Weekly Market Review
title: Weekly Market Review
text:
BOTTOM LINE — AI unwind week: tech cracked, defensives and energy absorbed the damage.
The week was a straight high-to-low rotation: semis and memory led the decline, staples and energy led the advance, and Friday's session accelerated the damage rather than reversing it. Small caps beat large by 0.78pp, but that is a relative win inside a losing tape — both were down. The dominant driver was positioning out of AI hardware, not a macro shock.

INDICES — DIA +0.58%, RSP +0.49%, SPY -1.97%, IWM -3.05%, QQQ -5.52%.
Style: small (-1.19%) outperformed large (-1.97%) by 0.78pp, though IJH -1.47% and IJR -1.19% still lost ground — the win was relative only. VIX closed at 20.0 versus a 20-day average of 15.7, so vol rose on the week. The week's most notable cross-asset move: WTI (USO) +2.83% Friday with crude stocks printing -855.7 (10k bbl) versus -28.8 forecast. QQQ and IWM sit below their 200-day MA; SPY is barely above it.

SECTORS & ROTATION — 1. XLP Staples +5.02%; 2. XLE Energy +4.86%; 3. XLV Health Care +3.45%; 4. XLB Materials +3.01%; 5. XLU Utilities +1.93%; 6. XLF Financials +1.44%; 7. XLRE Real Estate +1.32%; 8. XLC Comm Services -0.05%; 9. XLY Discretionary -0.35%; 10. XLI Industrials -0.88%; 11. XLK Tech -7.70%.
Industries: USO +9.15% and FCG +4.74% led; DRAM -18.78% and WGMI -22.24% were crushed. Money moved out of SMH (-650, 10th pctile) and DRAM (-1028, 0th pctile) into XLE (+662, 88th) and QQQ (+4541) — but QQQ's inflow against a -5.52% week is dip-buying, not confirmation. Rotation state: AI hardware fading / high-to-low rotation.

DRIVERS — Tech was the week's entire problem: XLK -7.70%, SOXX -11.80%, SMH -10.53%, DRAM -18.78%, with SOXX volume at 2.1x average and QQQ at 1.9x. Capital rotated into hard assets and defensives — XLP +5.02%, XLE +4.86%, GDX +304 (90th pctile) — while GLD bled -886 (15th pctile) and silver fell -5.97%. Macro prints support the energy bid: crude stocks -855.7 versus -28.8 forecast, PPI 1.3% m/m versus 0.5% forecast and 6.3% y/y, import prices 1.1% versus 0.8%. VVIX 109.9 (ma20 88.9) and VXN 27.1 (ma20 21.7) show vol being repriced in tech specifically, not broadly.

WHAT'S NEXT — FOMC is Oct 28, and Polymarket prices 80% odds of a 2026 hike, so the rate path stays live into the meeting. Watch whether SOXX stabilizes near its 200-day MA or whether DRAM's -18.78% week marks a positioning flush — SMH at the 10th percentile of 52-week flows is a contrarian tell. Breadth is the tell: only 45% of S&P names above their 50-day MA and 51% above the 200-day, so a defensives-led tape has room to keep running.
